comments.body:
Hi @zhaochenyang20, I'd like to take this issue.Could you assign it to me?

I'll start by reading through the existing checksum flow in PR #18306 and the loading paths for VAE and text encoder to understand exactly where disk names diverge from server-side parameter names. My initial impression is that VAE should be simpler (direct load_state_dict) and text encoder trickier (QKV stacking in load_weights), but I want to confirm before proposing a design.

One question: I don't have an A100 80G. Can I test with a smaller model like FLUX.2-klein-4B, or is there a recommended lightweight setup?

Just note for VAE, the following 3 named parameters might be added to model when loaded which are will not present in disk safetensor file, when computing the checksum, we need to take this into consideration. 

```
bn.num_batches_tracked
bn.running_mean
bn.running_var
```

Above is only a case for  FLUX.2-klein-4B, might worth checking other models.
I’ve run into some difficulties and won’t be able to continue. Anyone is welcome to take over. I apologize for the delay and any inconvenience.

title: [Feature] Compare the server-disk checksum in VAE and text encoder for update weights from disk of Diffusion models
